en: Bamboo is actually a giant grass, and some species can grow up to 91 centimeters in a single day.
Wombats produce cube-shaped poop to prevent it from rolling away, which helps them mark their territory on rocks and logs.
The hydrochloric acid in your human stomach is so strong that it can actually dissolve metal razor blades.
Periodical cicadas spend up to 17 years living underground as nymphs before emerging to mate and sing for just a few weeks.
Mangrove trees survive in salty ocean water because their specialized roots filter out up to 90 percent of the salt.
The axolotl, a type of salamander, can regenerate lost body parts, including its heart, brain, and even parts of its spinal cord.
The Venus flytrap counts the number of times an insect touches its trigger hairs before snapping shut to ensure a real meal.
Humans shed approximately 40,000 dead skin cells every single hour, meaning we completely replace our outer skin layer every month.
Parrotfish eat coral and excrete it as fine white sand, with one large fish producing hundreds of pounds of beach sand yearly.
The Welwitschia plant survives in the Namib Desert by absorbing moisture from coastal fog through its two continuously growing, strap-like leaves.
The wood frog can survive being completely frozen solid during winter because its body produces a natural antifreeze to protect its cells.
If you uncoiled all the DNA in your body, it would stretch to the sun and back hundreds of times.
